mainTopic: Guaranteeing and passing on loans with רבית involving a גוי, and whether a גוי has שליחות or זכיה
overview: The גמרא asks whose guarantor a Jew may be on a loan with רבית. It cannot be a Jewish lender, and a גוי lender seems forbidden too, since under his law he collects straight from the עָרֵב. רב ששת answers that the גוי agreed to Jewish rules for collecting the debt, but not to the ban on רבית. Next the גמרא quotes the משנה that a Jew may lend a גוי's money with the גוי's knowledge, and brings a ברייתא with two mirror-image cases of passing a loan on to another Jew. The גמרא challenges the permitted case: since אין שליחות לגוי, the first Jew seems to be taking רבית himself. רב הונא בר מנוח and then רב פפא explain the case so that the money goes directly from the גוי to the second Jew. רב אשי tries to limit אין שליחות לגוי in two different ways, and both are rejected through the פסוק ״גם אתם״. רבינא then suggests that a גוי has rabbinic זכיה, like a קטן, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Guarantor for whom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose guarantor a Jew may be on a loan with רבית, and first suggests a Jewish lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: A guarantor for whom? If you say a guarantor for a Jew…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which lender the earlier permission to be an עָרֵב is talking about. It suggests the first option, a Jewish lender, and is setting up a challenge to that option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible lenders, a Jew or a גוי. The גמרא will test each one to see whether being a guarantor for it is really allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarantor; the person who promises to pay if the borrower does not
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)

phrases.english: A guarantor for whom?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the earlier teaching that a Jew may be a guarantor on a loan with interest.

phrases.english: If you say a guarantor for a Jew,

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which lender, a Jew or a גוי, is the permitted guarantee for?

steps.title: A guarantor for a Jewish lender is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A משנה lists the עָרֵב among those who break the ban on רבית, so the first option fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: These transgress a negative commandment: the lender and the borrower, the guarantor and the witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first option. A משנה clearly says that a guarantor on a loan with רבית between Jews breaks a לא תעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the permission were about a Jewish lender, it would contradict this explicit משנה. So the permission cannot be about a Jew lending to a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introduces a source that contradicts the suggestion)

phrases.english: But it was taught:
phrases.notes: This is quoting a משנה later in this פרק (on 75b).

phrases.english: These transgress a negative commandment:
the lender and the borrower, the guarantor and the witnesses!

steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the permitted guarantee is for a Jewish lender
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit משנה names the עָרֵב as breaking the ban on רבית between Jews.

steps.title: A guarantor for a gentile lender also looks forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The second option, a גוי lender, also fails. Under the גוי's law the lender collects from the עָרֵב, so the guarantor ends up taking רבית from the Jewish borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a guarantor for a gentile. But since the gentile's law is that he goes after the guarantor, the guarantor is the one who takes the interest from him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, a גוי lender, and immediately raises a problem with it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the גוי's law, the lender goes straight to the guarantor for payment. That makes it as if the עָרֵב borrowed from the גוי and lent to the Jewish borrower. So the guarantor would be the one collecting רבית from a Jew, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the gentile (how a גוי court collects debts)

phrases.english: Rather, for a gentile.
But since the law of the gentile is
that he goes after the guarantor,
phrases.notes: Under the גוי's law, the lender can collect straight from the guarantor without first going to the borrower.

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ נִיהוּ דְּקָא שָׁקֵיל מִינֵּיהּ רִבִּיתָא!
phrases.english: he (the guarantor) is the one taking interest from him (the borrower)!

steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the permitted guarantee is for a גוי lender
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because גוי law sends the lender to collect from the עָרֵב, the guarantor is treated as the real lender who takes רבית from a Jew.

steps.title: רב ששת: the gentile agreed to Jewish law
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the case is where the גוי lender agreed to be judged by Jewish law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The case is where the gentile accepted upon himself to be judged by the laws of Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת saves the second option. The case is where the גוי agreed to follow Jewish law for this loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Jewish law, the lender must first try to collect from the borrower and cannot go straight to the עָרֵב. So the guarantor is only a backup, not the real lender, and he is not the one taking רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: To be judged by Jewish laws

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
The case is where he (the gentile) accepted upon himself to be judged by the laws of Jews.
phrases.notes: So the גוי cannot go straight to the guarantor. He has to collect from the borrower first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גוי collects from the עָרֵב under his own law, so the עָרֵב takes the רבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גוי agreed to Jewish law, so he must collect from the borrower first and the עָרֵב is only a backup.

steps.title: Then he should not take interest either
steps.stepSummary: If the גוי accepted Jewish law, he should also be bound by the Jewish ban on רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he accepted upon himself to be judged by the laws of Jews, he should not take interest either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's answer. If the גוי agreed to follow Jewish law, why may he still charge רבית?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jewish law forbids רבית. So if the גוי accepted Jewish law, it seems he should accept all of it, including that ban.

phrases.aramaic: אִי קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: If he accepted upon himself to be judged by the laws of Jews,
he should not take interest either!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's answer that the גוי accepted Jewish law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Accepting Jewish law should include its ban on רבית, so the loan should have no interest at all.

steps.title: He accepted one part of Jewish law but not the other
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the גוי accepted Jewish law only for how the debt is collected, not for the ban on רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: He accepted upon himself this, but did not accept upon himself that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains that the גוי agreed to only part of Jewish law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי accepted the Jewish rule about collection, so he must go to the borrower first. He did not accept the ban on רבית, so he may still charge interest. That leaves the Jewish עָרֵב permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And he did not accept upon himself

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew may be an עָרֵב for a גוי lender only when the גוי has agreed to collect by Jewish rules, going to the borrower first. The גוי may still charge רבית.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
He accepted upon himself this,
phrases.notes: "This" means the Jewish rule about collecting, where the lender goes to the borrower first.

phrases.english: and he did not accept upon himself that.
phrases.notes: "That" means the ban on taking interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ, וְלֹא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting Jewish law means accepting all of it, including the ban on רבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גוי accepted only the collection procedure, not the ban on רבית.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about lending a gentile's money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a Jew may lend a גוי's money with the גוי's knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A Jew may lend the money of a gentile with the knowledge of the gentile," etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and quotes it. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows a Jew to act as a middleman who lends a גוי's money to another Jew with interest, as long as it is done with the גוי's knowledge. It is not allowed with the knowledge of a Jew, meaning when the deal is really the middleman's own.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the quote continues

phrases.english: A Jew may lend the money of a gentile
with the knowledge of the gentile, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְוֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל מְעוֹתָיו שֶׁל נׇכְרִי מִדַּעַת הַנׇּכְרִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may lend a גוי's money to a Jew with interest when it is done with the גוי's knowledge.

steps.title: The ברייתא's case: passing on the loan yourself is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה with a case. A Jew who borrowed from a גוי with interest may not pass the money to another Jew for the same interest on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A Jew may lend a gentile's money with the gentile's knowledge, but not with a Jew's knowledge. How so? A Jew borrowed money with interest from a gentile and wanted to return it. Another Jew found him and said: Give it to me and I will pay you the way you pay him. This is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains what 'with a Jew's knowledge' means, using a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first borrower hands the money over on his own, without involving the גוי, he becomes the lender. The interest he collects is then רבית from one Jew to another, which is forbidden.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A Jew may lend the money of a gentile
with the knowledge of the gentile,
but not with the knowledge of a Jew.
phrases.notes: "A Jew" here means the middleman himself, acting on his own.

phrases.english: How so?

phrases.aramaic: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלָּוָה מָעוֹת מִן הַגּוֹי בְּרִבִּית
phrases.english: A Jew who borrowed money from a gentile with interest
and wanted to return it to him,
another Jew found him and said to him:
Give it to me, and I will pay you extra
the same way that you pay him extra,
it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַלְוֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל מְעוֹתָיו שֶׁל נׇכְרִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passing a borrowed גוי loan to another Jew on your own, for the same interest, is forbidden רבית between Jews.

steps.title: Bringing the second Jew to the gentile is permitted
steps.stepSummary: If the first borrower presents the second Jew to the גוי, the arrangement is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he presented him to the gentile, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the permitted version of the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the second Jew is brought to the גוי and the גוי agrees, the loan is now between the גוי and the second Jew. The interest goes to the גוי, so no Jew is collecting רבית from another Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: He presented him to the gentile

steps.whatToRemember: The difference is who the real lender is. If the Jewish middleman passes on the loan himself, it is forbidden. If the loan is set up directly with the גוי, it is permitted.

phrases.english: But if he presented him to the gentile,
phrases.notes: He brings the second Jew to the גוי, so the גוי himself becomes the lender.

phrases.english: it is permitted.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When the second Jew borrows directly from the גוי through the middleman's introduction, it is the גוי's loan and is permitted.

steps.title: A gentile borrower passes the loan to another Jew
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a reverse case. A גוי borrowed from a Jew with interest. Another Jew may take the money from the גוי and pay the גוי interest. But if the גוי presents him to the Jewish lender, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, a גוי borrowed money from a Jew with interest and wanted to pay it back. Another Jew met him and said: 'Give the money to me, and I will pay you interest just like you pay him.' This is permitted. But if the גוי brought him to the Jewish lender, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, mirror-image case: this time the גוי is the one who borrowed from a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second Jew deals only with the גוי, the second Jew pays interest to a גוי, not to a Jew, so it is allowed. If the גוי presents him to the Jewish lender, it looks like the lender is now lending to the second Jew with interest. That is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He presented him to, introduced him to

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In Steps 8–9 a Jew borrowed from a גוי. Here a גוי borrowed from a Jew. The rule flips: here, presenting the second Jew to the Jewish lender makes it forbidden.

phrases.english: And similarly, a gentile who borrowed money
from a Jew with interest
and wanted to return it to him
another Jew found him and said to him
Give it to me
and I will pay you
phrases.notes: He means he will pay the interest.

phrases.english: in the same way that you pay him – it is permitted
But if he presented him to the Jew – it is forbidden

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן גּוֹי שֶׁלָּוָה מָעוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּרִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a mirror-image case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may take over a גוי's loan from a Jew and pay the גוי interest, unless the גוי presents him to the Jewish lender.

steps.title: Since a gentile cannot be an agent, why is the first case allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The stricter ruling is understandable, but the lenient first case is hard. A גוי cannot be a שליח, so it seems the first Jew is really the one taking interest from the second Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last ruling makes sense as a stringency. But the first ruling is hard. There is no שליחות for a גוי, so isn't the Jew himself the one taking interest from the other Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lenient case from Step 9, where the first Jewish borrower presented the second Jew to the גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden ruling is easy to accept, because being strict is safe. But in the permitted case, the money passes from the first Jew to the second. A גוי cannot appoint a שליח, so the first Jew is not acting for the גוי. It looks like a direct loan with interest between two Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching
The first part of a teaching
A גוי cannot have an agent act for him in halacha

phrases.english: Granted the last clause, it is a stringency
But the first clause
phrases.notes: This is the earlier case (Step 9), where the first Jew presented the second Jew to the גוי, and it was allowed.

phrases.english: since there is no agency for a gentile

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ נִיהוּ דְּקָא שָׁקֵיל מִינֵּיהּ רִבִּיתָא?
phrases.english: isn't he the one who is taking interest from him?
phrases.notes: The first Jew is taking interest from the second Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the lenient ruling of the ברייתא now that both cases are on the table.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permitted case of the ברייתא (Step 9)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גוי cannot have a שליח. So the first Jew who hands over the money is acting for himself, making it a loan with interest between two Jews.

steps.title: The case is where the money was put on the ground
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח, quoting רב אחא בריה דרב איקא, says the case is where the גוי told the first Jew to put the money on the ground and be free of the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח said in the name of רב אחא the son of רב איקא: We are dealing with a case where the גוי told him, 'Put the money on the ground and be free.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The money never passes from one Jew's hand to the other's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first Jew puts the money down and is released from his debt to the גוי. The second Jew then picks it up, so he is borrowing straight from the גוי. No שליח is needed, so there is no loan between two Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Manoach said

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
phrases.english: in the name of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika
Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where he said to him
Put it on the ground and be released

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first Jew handed the money to the second, making him the lender.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first Jew put the money on the ground and was released, so the second Jew takes it directly from the גוי.

steps.title: Then why say something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: If the money was put on the ground, the first Jew is clearly out of the picture. So why does the ברייתא need to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's answer by saying it makes the ברייתא's ruling too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the first Jew drops the money and walks away, he plainly has nothing to do with the second loan. A ברייתא does not bother teaching something that obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (It is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר מנוח's explanation of the case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With the money on the ground, the ruling is obvious, so the ברייתא would have no reason to teach it.

steps.title: The gentile took the money and handed it over himself
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different case. The גוי himself took the money from the first Jew and gave it by hand to the second Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: The case is where the גוי took the money and gave it over with his own hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא shows the גמרא is dropping רב הונא's answer, and רב פפא offers a new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גוי takes the money from the first Jew and hands it himself to the second Jew. The loan is directly between the גוי and the second Jew, so no שליח is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it and gave it by hand

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said
For example, where he took and gave it by hand
phrases.notes: The גוי took the money from the first Jew and handed it to the second Jew himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in Step 13 with a new explanation of the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case needed money on the ground, which made it obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גוי himself passed the money to the second Jew, so the loan is directly from the גוי.

steps.title: This still seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: Even in רב פפא's case, the גוי clearly lends directly to the second Jew. So why teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question again: רב פפא's case also seems too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גוי hands the money over himself, the loan is plainly between the גוי and the second Jew. So the same question returns.

phrases.english: And still, what is there to say?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation of the case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A direct handoff by the גוי still makes the ruling obvious.

steps.title: The gentile is not lending because of the first Jew
steps.stepSummary: One might think the גוי lends only because he trusts the first Jew, which would make the first Jew part of the loan. The ברייתא teaches that this is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: When the גוי himself does this, he gives the money relying on the Jew. So the ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'it is obvious' question. It explains what mistake a learner might have made without this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the first Jew introduced the second, we might think the גוי lends only because of him. Then the first Jew would count as part of the loan, and it would be forbidden. The ברייתא teaches that the loan still belongs to the גוי alone, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Relying on, with the agreement of

steps.whatToRemember: The first case of the ברייתא is permitted only when the גוי himself hands the money to the second Jew. Even though the first Jew introduced them, the loan is from the גוי, so the second Jew pays interest to a גוי and not to a Jew.

phrases.english: You might have said
the gentile himself, when he does this
is deciding and giving on the strength of the Jew
it teaches us otherwise

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15 and backs רב פפא's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא – showing what mistake we might have made without the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גוי lends only because he trusts the first Jew, so the first Jew is part of the loan.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loan is from the גוי alone, so it is permitted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When the גוי personally hands the money to the second Jew, the loan is his, even though the first Jew introduced them.

steps.title: רב אשי limits 'no agency for a gentile' to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the rule אין שליחות לגוי applies only to תרומה. Everywhere else in the Torah, a גוי can be an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When we say a gentile cannot be an agent, that is only about תרומה. In every other area of the Torah, a gentile can be an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a new approach. He narrows the rule that a גוי cannot be a שליח so that it covers only תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 11 assumed אין שליחות לגוי is a general rule. רב אשי says it applies only to separating תרומה, so in a loan the first Jew can act as the גוי's שליח. That means the loan is really the גוי's, and the permitted case of the ברייתא makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Agency: one person acting on behalf of another
A gentile cannot act as a legal agent
The portion of produce given to a כהן
This applies only to... (a limiting phrase)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When we say there is no agency for a gentile,
that applies only to terumah,
but in the whole rest of the Torah,
there is agency for a gentile.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כִּי אָמְרִינַן אֵין שְׁלִיחוּת לְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of step 11: if a גוי can have a שליח, the first Jew acts as the גוי's agent, so the ברייתא's permitted case works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אין שליחות לגוי is a general rule across the whole Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב אשי, the rule is limited to תרומה.

steps.title: רב אשי's limit is called a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא calls רב אשי's view a mistake. It first explains where the תרומה rule comes from: ״גם אתם״ teaches that agents must be בני ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement of רב אשי is a mistake. Why can't a gentile be an agent for תרומה? Because the verse says 'you' and then 'you also.' Just as you are members of the covenant, your agents must be members of the covenant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אשי. It starts by showing the source for why a גוי cannot be a שליח for תרומה, and it sets up the next line, which completes the rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word ״גם״ in ״גם אתם״ adds agents: an agent can separate תרומה for you. The comparison 'like you' means the agent must be a בן ברית, just like the owner. So a גוי is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You also': the פסוק about separating תרומה
Members of the covenant, meaning Jews

phrases.english: And this statement of Rav Ashi is a mistake:
What is different about terumah, that a gentile cannot be an agent for it?
Because it is written 'you' — 'you also':
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:28. The extra word 'also' is read as adding agents.

phrases.english: just as you are members of the covenant,
so too your agents must also be members of the covenant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting רב אשי's limitation by examining the source of the תרומה rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב אשי's attempt to limit אין שליחות לגוי to תרומה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source of the תרומה rule is the same source that all agency depends on (completed in the next step).

steps.title: All agency is learned from תרומה, so the limit fails
steps.stepSummary: Agency for the whole Torah is learned from תרומה. So the בני ברית requirement applies everywhere, and רב אשי's view is a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Agency for the whole Torah is also learned from תרומה. So רב אשי's statement is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its argument. Since all שליחות comes from the תרומה source, the restriction to בני ברית comes along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי wanted to separate תרומה from the rest of the Torah. But the very idea that agency works at all is learned from תרומה. You can't take agency from there without also taking its condition that the agent must be a בן ברית.
steps.whatToRemember: All שליחות in the Torah is learned from the תרומה פסוק ״גם אתם״, so its requirement that the agent be a בן ברית applies everywhere.

phrases.english: Agency for the whole Torah,
we also learn it from terumah.
Rather, Rav Ashi's statement is a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלִיחוּת דְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ נָמֵי מִתְּרוּמָה גָּמְרִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since all agency comes from תרומה, a גוי cannot be a שליח anywhere in the Torah. רב אשי's limitation is rejected.

steps.title: Second version: a Jew can be an agent for a gentile
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב אשי says the rule only stops a גוי from being a שליח for a Jew. A Jew can still be a שליח for a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב אשי said this instead: When we say there is no agency for a gentile, that means they cannot be agents for us. But we can be agents for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רב אשי's statement. This time he limits the rule by direction, not by topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב אשי accepts that a גוי cannot act for a Jew. But he says the reverse still works: a Jew can act as a שליח on behalf of a גוי.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion stacked on top of the first one. It is a different report of what רב אשי said.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Ashi said:
When we say there is no agency for a gentile,
that applies to them acting for us,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֲנַן לְדִידְהוּ הָוֵינָא לְהוּ שְׁלִיחַ.
phrases.english: but we can be agents for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of רב אשי's statement from Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי cannot be a שליח for a Jew, but a Jew can be a שליח for a גוי.

steps.title: The second version is also called a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this version too, using the same פסוק. ״גם אתם״ ties agency to בני ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement of רב אשי is also a mistake. Why can't they be agents for us? Because the verse says 'you' and 'you also,' to include your agents. Just as you are members of the covenant, your agents are members of the covenant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second version of רב אשי with the same source it used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason a גוי cannot act for us is the פסוק ״גם אתם״, which compares 'you', the senders, to 'your agents': both are בני ברית. This step gives that source. The next step uses the same comparison to show that a Jew cannot act for a גוי either.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (an extra word adds something)

phrases.english: And this statement of Rav Ashi is a mistake,
for what is different about them acting for us, that they cannot?
Because it is written 'you,' 'you also':
phrases.notes: The same פסוק as before, במדבר 18:28.

phrases.english: to include your agents:
just as you are members of the covenant,
so too your agents are members of the covenant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second version of רב אשי from Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that a Jew can be a שליח for a גוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source for agency, ״גם אתם״, frames all agency as happening between בני ברית, so it cannot work in either direction with a גוי.

steps.title: A Jew cannot be an agent for a גוי either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out why the second version of רב אשי fails. The פסוק ״גם אתם״ requires the sender to be a בן ברית, so a Jew cannot act as a שליח for a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We cannot be agents for them either, because the פסוק says: just as you (the senders) are members of the covenant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the rejection from step 21. It explains that the problem is not only who the agent is, but also who sends him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second version of רב אשי said a Jew may still act for a גוי. The גמרא answers that ״אתם״ refers to the people who appoint the agent, and they must be בני ברית. A גוי cannot appoint a שליח at all, so a Jew cannot be his agent.

keyTerms.meaning: just as you; the senders are being compared to the agents
members of the covenant, meaning Jews

steps.confusionAlert: It is easy to think the rule only says who can be an agent. The גמרא here says the rule works in both directions: the sender and the agent must both be בני ברית.

phrases.english: We, too, cannot be agents for them,
for it says: just as you are members of the covenant!
phrases.notes: This is the reading of ״גם אתם״ (במדבר 18:28) from step 18. The people sending must be Jews too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן לְדִידְהוּ נָמֵי, מָה אַתֶּם בְּנֵי בְרִית קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the full reasoning behind the rejection begun in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The second version of רב אשי, which allows a Jew to be a שליח for a גוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that ״אתם״ also requires the sender to be a בן ברית, so a גוי cannot send any agent.

steps.title: The second version of רב אשי is also a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this version of רב אשי's view is also an error.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this statement of רב אשי is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion of רב אשי. Both versions of his view have been rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the גמרא called the first version a mistake. Now it says the same about the second version. Neither version holds up against ״גם אתם״.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of רב אשי fail. ״גם אתם״ teaches that שליחות only works between בני ברית, both as agent and as sender.

phrases.english: Rather, this statement of Rav Ashi
is a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּרַב אָשֵׁי בְּרוּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the rejection in step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's second version is rejected as well. A גוי has no part in שליחות in either direction.

steps.title: רבינא: a גוי has rabbinic זכיה, like a קטן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא offers a new approach. A גוי cannot use שליחות, but the רבנן gave him the power of זכיה, as they did for a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Granted, a גוי has no agency. But he does have the power to acquire by rabbinic law. This is just like a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רב אשי's approach is gone, רבינא gives a different way to make the case work. He uses זכיה instead of שליחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא accepts that a גוי has no שליחות. He argues that זכיה is a separate tool, and the רבנן allowed a גוי to have it, so the arrangement can still work. He backs this up by comparing it to a קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: acquiring an item on someone's behalf, even without being his agent
it is just like; introduces a comparison

steps.confusionAlert: זכיה and שליחות are not the same thing. רבינא admits a גוי has no שליחות. He says only that the רבנן gave him זכיה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new path. A transaction can sometimes work through rabbinic זכיה even where Torah-level שליחות is impossible.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Granted that a gentile has no agency,
he does have acquisition by rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: He means that someone else can acquire something for the גוי, even though he cannot appoint an agent.

phrases.english: just as is the case with a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: נְהִי דִּשְׁלִיחוּת לְגוֹי לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב אשי's rejected answer with a new mechanism, זכיה מדרבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New legal mechanism: rabbinic זכיה instead of שליחות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a גוי has no שליחות at all, nothing can be acquired for him through another person.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי has no שליחות, but the רבנן gave him זכיה, as they did for a קטן.

steps.title: Starting the comparison to a קטן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא begins explaining the comparison: a קטן has no שליחות. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not true of a minor that even though he has no agency...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבינא is starting to prove his point from the case of a קטן, and the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the proof is stated here: a קטן cannot make a שליח. The second half, which comes next, will show that he still has זכיה. That is exactly the pattern רבינא claims for a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: a minor, a child under the age of מצוות
is it not so? (a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: A minor: is it not so that even though
he has no agency,

steps.triggerLanguage: קָטָן לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ שְׁלִיחוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins backing up the comparison to a קטן that רבינא made in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that a גוי has זכיה מדרבנן without having שליחות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law of a קטן, who has no שליחות but does have זכיה (this part is completed on the next amud).
